reply_text:
㊥ (what the refusal says) The refusal reports a gap in the record, not a problem with your answer. The agreement route (`agreement_record.clj:70`) only looks for stored offer records on this seat. It never reads my reply text. So when I ask "Shall I…?" without also posting an offer, the route finds nothing, logs `no-visible-offer`, and stops. As you say, `🈸:yes` straight after a single "Shall I…?" can only mean one thing. The fault is that the route ignores the text it's answering. I was wrong to describe it as my 🈸 failing to post something.

🈖 (why it's built that way) Offers were designed as explicit records, made with `POST /api/alpha/offer`, so that an agreement names exactly what was agreed. The mission work item "Agents post an offer for each 🈸" was meant to fill the gap from the agent side, but it relies on every agent remembering to post. In practice none of my asks today posted one, so all your `🈸:yes` answers were refused. Even so, the work went ahead, because I read your yes from the text.

㊭ (fix on the reading side) When no stored offer is visible, resolve `🈸:yes` against the agent's previous reply:
- **One 🈸 paragraph:** that paragraph becomes the offer. The route records it, then records the agreement. The evidence is my reply and your turn.
- **Several 🈸 paragraphs:** the answer is ambiguous, as now. You'd answer with the number or offer id.
- **None:** the refusal stays as it is.

This keeps "an agreement names what was agreed": the text of the 🈸 paragraph is what gets named. It also means agents don't have to remember an extra step. It touches the live agreement code, `agreement_record.clj` plus the caller that knows the previous reply. It would also make the M-aif-over-the-operator work item mostly unnecessary, which the mission should record.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I make that change, with tests for the one, several and none cases?

previous_reply_acts.text: (what the gap means) The skeleton reads an unknown question as "asked before the window". That's the right default for a ledger excerpt, but it can't tell "asked earlier" from "never asked". To catch your refused agreements, the window would need to say "nothing before this point", so that any answer without its question is a finding. That's a small addition: a flag on `ingest` that turns those inputs into a finding. It's the same thing the mission's response projector needs, an explicit statement that no response arrived. I haven't made the change.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (the live version) Your pipeline, operator → 象 → agent, would make 象's reading of your turn, including the patterns it accepted or rejected, part of what I receive. I could then choose my marks knowing how the turn was read. In these models that adds one act between each J and C, which is easy to represent. It's harder to reason about, because my marks would then partly answer 象 rather than you. Holding it back is sensible. If it happens later, this flow, re-run with that extra act, shows what changes.
